name: Meridian Gondola
description: In the older waterfront districts where canals were built into the city infrastructure, electric gondolas serve as water taxis and tour boats. They're slow, scenic, and weirdly peaceful in a city that is neither of those things. The gondoliers are an institution — some families have been poling boats through these canals for three generations. The canals themselves are aging and in some districts slowly sinking, making the gondola routes change year by year as old channels flood and new ones form.
armament: None. The pole has traditional secondary uses.
common_usage: Canal district transit, tourism, romantic outings, the only way to reach certain waterfront addresses.
story_hooks: A gondolier navigates a canal that wasn't there yesterday — the water has broken through into a previously sealed underground passage
The gondolier families know the canal system so well they serve as an intelligence network, reporting on what they see from the water
physical_description: A narrow, flat-bottomed electric gondola stretches roughly 8 meters, its hull patched with decades of repairs—welded steel, composite patches, and worn wood railings stained by canal water and industrial runoff. The cabin is enclosed in weathered polycarbonate and corroded aluminum frames, with strings of faded LED strips running along the interior. A worn pole lies across the stern, though most modern versions rely on a quiet electric motor hidden beneath the waterline, its battery pack visible as a bulging compartment along the keel.
visual_prompt: Narrow electric gondola moored in rain-slicked canal, worn steel hull with welded patches, faded LED strips inside weathered polycarbonate cabin, industrial waterfront backdrop, neo-noir gritty aesthetic, moody cinematic lighting, detailed product photography, dark water reflection, rust and age visible, cyberpunk near-future setting
